newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas untraded as cricket stops play.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas untraded as cricket stops play.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market harked back to the quiet days of last week on Thursday, as once again no deals were done and only a smattering of bids and offers were posted by the close of trade.

But this time, traders said, there was an excuse: the gas trading community has moved en masse to Headingley, Leeds, to watch the first one day cricket international between England and Australia, and trading on both physical and futures markets has dried up.

By the close of trade, June was bid at 11.25 pence a therm and offered at 11.70 pence, the same position as at the close of the morning session. The only other months to see both bids and offers were January and May, with a 2.00 pence bid/offer spread in each case. January was in the range 16.50/18.50 pence a therm, with May at 10.00/12.00 pence.
The June bid was higher than Wednesday's settlement level, while in January and May bids and offers straddled the previous settlement price.
The contract traded 100 lots in each of the last two days and 45 lots on Monday.
